README: Researched answers, keyed by the question's row in the source spreadsheet so each entry can be checked against it. Every entry must cite a source; nothing is scored on inference alone. `basis` is 'national' where the evidence is specific to that country, or 'directive-baseline' where an EU instrument creates the right and national transposition has not been individually verified.

eu-2019-944-art11.title: Directive (EU) 2019/944, Article 11 - Entitlement to a dynamic electricity price contract

eu-2019-944-annex1.title: Directive (EU) 2019/944, Annex I - Minimum requirements for billing, with the three price components defined by Regulation (EU) 2016/1952

eu-2019-944-art23.title: Directive (EU) 2019/944, Articles 20–23 - Smart metering functionality and access to metering and consumption data

eu-2019-944-art17.title: Directive (EU) 2019/944, Article 17 - Demand response through aggregation

eu-2019-944-art32.title: Directive (EU) 2019/944, Article 32 - Incentives for the use of flexibility in distribution networks

ceer-art32-derogations.title: CEER - NRAs' approach to DSO flexibility procurement, justifications for derogations from Article 32

eu-red2-art17.title: Directive (EU) 2018/2001 (RED II), Article 17 - Simple-notification procedure for grid connections

eu-red2-art18.title: Directive (EU) 2018/2001 (RED II), Article 18(3) and Annex IV - Certification schemes for installers of small-scale renewable systems

eu-customs-cer.title: EU Common Customs Tariff - 0% duty on photovoltaic modules; 2.7% on lithium-ion batteries

au-aemc-smart-meters.title: AEMC - Accelerating smart meter deployment: final rule, 28 November 2024, universal deployment across the NEM by 2030

au-cheaper-home-batteries.title: DCCEEW - Cheaper Home Batteries Program, delivered through the Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme from 1 July 2025

au-aemc-export-tariffs.title: AEMC - Access, pricing and incentive arrangements for distributed energy resources, final determination 12 August 2021; AER Export Tariff Guidelines

au-saa-accreditation.title: Solar Accreditation Australia - installer and designer accreditation scheme operator under the SRES since 29 February 2024, enforcing AS/NZS 4777.2:2020

au-cer-installers.title: Clean Energy Regulator - rooftop solar installers and designers must hold SAA accreditation to create certificates under the SRES

au-aemo-dashboard.title: AEMO - NEM data dashboard: five-minute dispatch and FCAS prices, demand, generation and interconnector flows, published free and publicly since the five-minute settlement start on 1 October 2021

au-aemo-ancillary.title: AEMO - Ancillary services: eight separate FCAS markets in the NEM, accessible to aggregated small resources through registered aggregators

au-aemo-rert.title: AEMO - Reliability and Emergency Reserve Trader: availability and activation payments for curtailable load, including aggregated smaller loads, procured through a pre-qualified panel

au-aer-ringfencing.title: AER - Electricity Distribution Ring-fencing Guideline version 3 (3 November 2021): distributors prohibited from providing contestable services with a battery absent a waiver

au-csip-aus.title: CSIP-AUS - Common Smart Inverter Profile Australia, an IEEE 2030.5 based DER communications profile developed by the DER Integration API Technical Working Group, with CEC-certified inverters

au-aemo-sa-demand.title: AEMO - South Australian Electricity Report: record minimum operational demand of −209 MW on 19 October 2024, with rooftop PV meeting 64% of SA demand

au-saa-pathways.title: Solar Accreditation Australia - accreditation pathways built on nationally recognised UEE units (UEERE0054, UEERE0061, UEERE0080, UEERE0081), delivered by registered training organisations across Australia

au-import-tariffs.title: Australia - 0% import duty on solar panels and photovoltaic modules (GST applies separately); US ITA country commercial guide on Australian import tariffs

us-ferc-2222.title: FERC Order No. 2222 - requires RTOs/ISOs to let DER aggregations provide all wholesale services they are technically capable of; FERC explainer

us-ferc-2222-tracker.title: FERC Order 2222 DER policy and implementation tracker, January 2026 - PJM energy and ancillary services implementation 1 February 2028, SPP Q2 2030, ISO-NE capacity from FCA 19 in February 2026

us-irs-obbba.title: IRS - FAQs on modification of sections 25C, 25D and others under Public Law 119-21 (One Big Beautiful Bill, 4 July 2025): section 25D terminated for expenditures after 31 December 2025

us-doe-trade.title: US Department of Energy - Overview of trade and policy measures for US solar manufacturing (Section 201, Section 301 and AD/CVD orders)

us-section201-expiry.title: Solar Power World - Section 201 safeguard tariffs on imported solar panels expired 6 February 2026, having stepped down to 14% for 2025; AD/CVD orders on Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam imposed 24 June 2025 remain

us-irec-1547.title: IREC - IEEE 1547-2018 adoption tracker: state-by-state dates for requiring UL 1741 SB certified inverters in new interconnection applications

us-nrel-1547.title: NREL - Overview of distributed energy resource interconnection: IEEE 1547-2018 and UL 1741 certification of inverters

ca-nem3.title: California Net Billing Tariff (NEM 3.0) - approved by the CPUC 15 December 2022, effective 15 April 2023, replacing retail-rate net metering with hourly avoided-cost export compensation for PG&E, SCE and SDG&E customers (secondary source)

ca-sgip.title: California Self-Generation Incentive Program (SGIP) - CPUC-administered storage rebates of $200–$1,000/kWh; as of April 2026 the residential budgets are fully reserved and new applications are waitlisted (secondary source)

ca-rule21-ica.title: IREC - California adopts first interconnection rules to use hosting capacity results: Integration Capacity Analysis built into Rule 21, with monthly-updated public ICA maps from PG&E, SCE and SDG&E

ny-vder.title: NYSERDA - Value of Distributed Energy Resources (VDER) Value Stack: compensation by when and where a DER delivers, comprising energy, capacity, environmental, demand reduction and locational system relief value

ny-sir.title: NY Department of Public Service - New York State Standardized Interconnection Requirements, effective 1 August 2025: a single statewide process for distributed generation and storage up to 5 MW

ny-sun.title: NYSERDA - NY-Sun megawatt block incentive: regional blocks of capacity funded at declining rates, available until each block is fully subscribed

us-irec-hca.title: IREC - The evolution of hosting capacity analysis as a grid modernization tool: California, Nevada, Minnesota, New York, Maryland, New Jersey and Connecticut require utilities to publish solar hosting capacity maps; Hawaii also mandates hosting capacity analyses

tx-ercot-ader.title: ERCOT - Aggregate Distributed Energy Resource (ADER) pilot project, in Phase 3 as of 2025, letting aggregated distribution-level resources respond to ERCOT dispatch

tx-no-net-metering.title: pv magazine USA - no Texas utility offers statewide net metering for rooftop solar; some retailers offer lower-value buyback and Denton Municipal Electric is a lone exception

hi-smart-der.title: Hawaiian Electric - Smart Renewable Energy (Smart DER) export programme approved by the Hawaii PUC, with Customer Grid Supply, CGS Plus and Smart Export customers transitioning to Smart DER export tracks from 1 October 2024

hi-byod.title: Hawaiian Electric - Bring Your Own Device and BYOD Plus (from 15 May 2025) pay solar-plus-storage customers to discharge at peak; the earlier Battery Bonus programme closed to new participants on 1 July 2024

ma-smart.title: Massachusetts SMART (Solar Massachusetts Renewable Target) programme - per-kWh incentive paid for 20 years on top of net metering (secondary source)

ma-connectedsolutions.title: Mass Save ConnectedSolutions - performance-based battery demand response paying roughly $225/kW of average summer performance across 30–60 dispatch events (secondary source)

in-surya-ghar.title: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana - announced 15 February 2024: ₹30,000/kW up to 2 kW and ₹18,000/kW above, capped at ₹78,000 for residential rooftop solar, with DISCOM approval and net metering (secondary source)

in-customs.title: Energetica India - Union Budget 2025-26 cut basic customs duty on solar cells and modules to 20%, effective 2 February 2025; a 20% AIDC applies on top, and DGTR recommended anti-dumping duties of up to 30% on Chinese cells and modules in September 2025

pk-nepra.title: NEPRA (Alternative & Renewable Energy) Distributed Generation and Net Metering Regulations 2015, revised December 2025: new prosumers move to net billing at a fixed Rs11/unit export rate against Rs22 for existing seven-year agreements, with agreement terms cut to five years

bd-net-metering.title: Bangladesh Net Metering Guidelines 2018 (amended 2019) - SREDA framework requiring bi-directional, time-of-use capable meters and SREDA-approved equipment meeting Bangladesh Standards and equivalent IEC standards

lk-soorya-bala.title: Soorya Bala Sangramaya (Battle for Solar Energy) - Ministry of Power and Renewable Energy with SLSEA, CEB and LECO, offering rooftop customers a choice of Net Metering, Net Accounting or Net Plus

hi-shift-and-save.title: Hawaiian Electric - Shift and Save time-of-use rates (daytime, evening peak and overnight priced roughly 1:2:3), launched as a 16,000-customer pilot on Oʻahu and Hawaiʻi Island and closed to new enrolments from 1 February 2025

ma-interconnection.title: Commonwealth of Massachusetts - utility interconnection: the DPU requires all investor-owned distribution companies to interconnect distributed generation under a common Model DG Interconnection Tariff with Simplified and Expedited processes

acer-ceer-retail-2024.title: ACER/CEER - 2024 Market Monitoring Report on Energy Retail and Consumer Protection: fewer than 30% of households can access dynamic price contracts in 10 member states, and fixed or regulated contracts still dominate at household level in 15

de-kfw-270.title: KfW programme 270 'Erneuerbare Energien – Standard' - promotional loan covering 100% of PV and battery investment, terms to 30 years, rates from about 3.98% effective (secondary source)

de-eeg-fit.title: Germany EEG feed-in tariff - remuneration fixed for 20 years from commissioning, with separate rates for surplus feed-in and full feed-in; pv magazine on the August 2025 revision

de-mastr.title: Bundesnetzagentur - Marktstammdatenregister (core energy market data register): free online registration of every generating installation, required within one month of commissioning under §71 EEG 2023 and a precondition for EEG remuneration

fr-autoconsommation.title: France - the prime à l'autoconsommation was abolished for new surplus-sale installations in early June 2026, and EDF OA surplus buyback fell to 1.1 c€/kWh HT from 5 June 2026 (previously 4 c€/kWh); photovoltaic panels are not covered by MaPrimeRénov' (secondary source)

it-detrazione.title: Italy - 50% income tax deduction on photovoltaic installation up to €96,000 for a first home through 31 December 2026, 36% for other properties, spread over ten annual instalments (secondary source)

it-ritiro-dedicato.title: Italy - Scambio sul Posto closed to plants commissioned from 29 May 2025; Ritiro Dedicato with the GSE is the route for new installations, with a 2026 minimum guaranteed price of 4.75 c€/kWh (secondary source)

es-rd244.title: Spain - Real Decreto 244/2019 self-consumption framework: simplified surplus compensation nets exports against imports within a billing period for renewable installations up to 100 kW, with registration in the self-consumption registry and notification to the distributor; IDAE grants cover 15–40% of cost (secondary source)

nl-saldering.title: Rijksoverheid - the salderingsregeling ends on 1 January 2027 in a single step; households net exports against consumption until 31 December 2026, after which suppliers must pay a feed-in compensation of at least 50% of the basic supply tariff until 2030

pl-moj-prad.title: Mój Prąd - NFOŚiGW prosumer support programme: up to 7,000 PLN for a 2–10 kWp PV system and up to 16,000 PLN for storage under edition 6.0, with settlement under net-billing a condition of the grant

pl-net-billing.title: Poland net-billing - prosumers sell surplus at the market price published by URE and buy at the retail price, replacing the earlier net-metering discount system (secondary source)

ke-net-metering-2024.title: Kenya - The Energy (Net-Metering) Regulations 2024, gazetted by the Cabinet Secretary for Energy to operationalise section 162 of the Energy Act 2019: renewable systems under 1 MW, domestic installations capped at 10 kW, a 60-day approval window and bill credits at the retail tariff (Bowmans legal briefing)

ke-epra-licensing.title: Kenya - EPRA Solar PV licensing: designers, installers, importers and vendors require an EPRA licence and technicians must register with the Engineers Board of Kenya, holding a T3 solar technician certificate; EPRA's service charter allows 60 days for technician licences (secondary source)

ke-import-standards.title: Kenya - Importation Guidelines for Solar PV Products and Systems (ACE-TAF/KEREA): KEBS Certificate of Conformity required per consignment, modules to KS IEC 61215 and KS IEC 61730

ke-import-duty.title: Kenya - solar modules (HS 8541.40) enter duty-free and VAT-exempt, while balance-of-system components are assessed separately: inverters (HS 8504.40) attract 10% duty and 16% VAT (secondary source)

jp-fit-2026.title: Japan - METI FIT terms for small and rooftop PV from FY2026: residential under 10 kW at ¥24/kWh for years 1–4 then ¥8.3/kWh to year 10; rooftop above 10 kW at ¥19/kWh for years 1–5 then ¥8.3/kWh to year 20, with a ¥1/kWh bonus at 30% or more self-consumption (pv magazine)

kr-support.title: South Korea - Korea Energy Agency new and renewable energy equipment fund offering concessional finance for projects up to 200 kW (raised from 100 kW in 2025), alongside the Solar Rental Program of low-interest loans and subsidies for residential and small commercial systems (secondary source)

kr-net-metering.title: South Korea - KEPCO net metering for systems up to 50 kW residential and 1 MW commercial, compensating surplus at retail rates under a grid connection agreement with the local KEPCO distribution subsidiary (secondary source)

id-memr-2-2024.title: Indonesia - MEMR Regulation No. 2 of 2024 on rooftop solar: net metering abolished so exports to PLN no longer reduce the bill, and development capped by a quota of 5,746 MW across 2024–2028; existing users approved before the regulation keep net metering for ten years (SSEK legal briefing)

id-iesr.title: IESR - MEMR Regulation No. 2/2024 limits public participation in the energy transition through rooftop solar, with the quota system and loss of net metering assessed as barriers to the 3.6 GW rooftop target

my-nem3.title: SEDA Malaysia - Net Energy Metering 3.0: export credit against the TNB bill, allocated by quota released in rounds, so approval does not follow automatically from application

eu-entsoe-transparency.title: Commission Regulation (EU) No 543/2013 on submission and publication of data in electricity markets - the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform, live since 5 January 2015, publishes TSO-submitted generation, load, transmission and balancing data free of charge, in English, downloadable and retained for at least five years

eu-red3-art16.title: Directive (EU) 2023/2413 (RED III), Article 16 - maximum permitting timeline of three months for rooftop solar, with tacit approval and refusals required to be explicit and reasoned

eu-epbd-solar-ready.title: EPBD recast (Directive (EU) 2024/1275) - new buildings permitted after 29 May 2026 must be designed to accommodate solar, with fast-track approval for systems up to 100 kW decided within one month (secondary source)

eu-reseu-schemes.title: RES EU certification - database of the certification schemes and qualifications required for small-scale renewable energy installers across European countries, maintained to support mutual recognition under RED II Annex IV

eu-2019-944-art36.title: Directive (EU) 2019/944, Article 36 - distribution system operators shall not own, develop, manage or operate energy storage facilities, save by derogation for fully integrated network components or where the regulator finds no market interest

gb-mcs-recc.title: MCS MIS 3002:2025 solar PV standard and the Renewable Energy Consumer Code - installers must calculate expected annual generation using the MCS Performance Estimate methodology, and every MCS-certified installer must belong to an approved consumer code covering sales practice, contracts and accurate performance estimates

gb-mcs-standard.title: MCS - MIS 3002 Solar PV Systems standard (v5.0, 2025): installation, wiring, commissioning and handover requirements aligned to BS 7671, including documentation of shading and yield

il-net-metering.title: Illinois - full retail net metering closed to new residential and small commercial interconnections from 1 January 2025, replaced by supply-only net metering; existing customers grandfathered unless they take the Distributed Generation rebate (secondary source)

il-dg-rebate.title: Illinois Shines - ComEd and Ameren Distributed Generation (smart inverter) rebate of $300/kW DC for solar and $300/kWh for battery storage, available to residential customers installing a grid-interactive inverter

az-net-billing.title: Arizona - net billing export rates set annually by the Arizona Corporation Commission on the Resource Comparison Proxy since 2017, locked for ten years at installation and limited to a 10% annual reduction: about $0.069/kWh (APS) and $0.051/kWh (TEP) in 2026 (secondary source)

az-hb2301.title: Arizona HB2301 - every municipality and county must offer instant solar permitting from 1 January 2026, with Phoenix, Tucson, Maricopa County and Mesa accepting SolarAPP+ for same-day residential PV permits (secondary source)

in-suryaghar-portal.title: PM Surya Ghar national portal - applications are submitted online and routed to the consumer's DISCOM for feasibility approval, with vendors registering on the portal and required to show at least three technicians trained under Suryamitra or SCGJ (secondary source)

lk-slsea-providers.title: Sri Lanka Sustainable Energy Authority - registered Solar PV Service Provider scheme: providers must register with SLSEA, submit test certificates from accredited laboratories and obtain SLSEA conformity certificates for panels, inverters and DC cables, under published rooftop installation guidelines

tx-interconnection-permits.title: Texas - grid-tied solar requires a municipal permit costing roughly $50–$500 depending on system size and jurisdiction, plus an interconnection agreement with the TDU (Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas), typically 15–30 business days for residential systems under 10 kW (secondary source)

tx-solar-rights.title: Texas Property Code §202.010 (Solar Rights Act) - property owners' associations may not prohibit a solar energy device, and any governing provision that does is void; HB 431 (2025) extended the definition to solar roof tiles. Reasonable aesthetic conditions remain permitted

eu-jrc-pv-standards.title: JRC - Standards for Photovoltaic Energy Systems: EN IEC 61215 for module design qualification and type approval, EN IEC 62109 for converter safety, and HD/IEC 60364-7-712 for the electrical installation of PV systems in buildings

eu-lvd-harmonised.title: EU - EN IEC 61730-1 and 61730-2 adopted as harmonised standards under the Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU through publication in the Official Journal; PV modules above 75 V DC also fall under the EMC Directive 2014/30/EU and RoHS 2011/65/EU (secondary source)

ca-csa-c22-1.title: Canada - CSA C22.1 (Canadian Electrical Code, Part I) Section 64 governs renewable energy systems, setting PV system voltage limits and wiring methods; all equipment must carry a certification mark from a Standards Council of Canada accredited body (secondary source)

ca-greener-homes.title: CMHC / Natural Resources Canada - the Canada Greener Homes Loan ($40,000 interest-free over ten years) closed to new applications on 2 October 2025; the $800m Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program launched September 2025 targets low- to median-income households and is delivered through the provinces, with solar eligibility varying by province

ca-net-metering.title: Canada - all nine provinces and three territories operate net metering (called micro-generation in Alberta and Yukon), with caps ranging from 10 kW in Nunavut to 5 MW under Alberta's Micro-Generation Regulation; BC Hydro credits at 1:1 retail monthly with annual surplus paid at wholesale (secondary source)

in-iex.title: Indian Energy Exchange - day-ahead and real-time market clearing prices and volumes published daily; 15-minute real-time block data available from 1 April 2022, regulated by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission since 2008 (secondary source)

in-cea-bis.title: India - CEA (Technical Standards for Connectivity of the Distributed Generation Resources) Regulations 2013 and CEA (Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations 2010 set grid connection requirements; BIS IS 16221 (inverters) and IS 14086 (modules, mandatory under the 2022 Quality Control Order) set equipment safety (secondary source)

in-net-metering-caps.title: India - rooftop solar capacity is generally capped at or below the sanctioned load, with state DISCOMs setting their own limits: most allow up to 100% of sanctioned load for residential, but Kerala proposed a 3 kW cap and other states vary considerably (secondary source)

pk-net-metering-timeline.title: Pakistan - net metering applications must be submitted through an AEDB-registered installer and take 30–90 days from application to commissioning depending on the DISCO and documentation completeness (secondary source)

pk-standards.title: Pakistan - NEPRA and DISCOs require IEC 61215/61730 certified panels and inverters compliant with IEEE 1547/UL 1741/IEC 62116 with mandatory anti-islanding; installers must hold AEDB competency certification (Category V1/V2) and Pakistan Engineering Council registration (secondary source)

lk-standards-detail.title: Sri Lanka - CEB's Guide for Grid Interconnection of Embedded Generators requires modules to IEC 61215/61730 and inverters to IEEE 1547/UL 1741 or IEC 62109, with commissioning tested against IEC 61727, IEEE 1547-2018 and the IET 18th Edition wiring regulations

bd-net-metering-timeline.title: Bangladesh - distribution utilities (BPDB, BREB, DESCO, DPDC and others) issue a net metering approval letter within 10 working days of application, sign the final agreement within 15 working days of a successful inspection, and give installers up to 8 months to complete the system (secondary source)

bd-training-sporadic.title: Bangladesh - solar PV training runs through occasional workshops (e.g. the Alliance for Rural Electrification's CORE microgrid design workshop, February 2025) and short private courses rather than a standing nationwide programme (secondary source)

za-tax-rebate-expired.title: South Africa - SARS residential solar tax rebate: 25% of panel cost up to R15,000, available only for panels first brought into use in the 2024 year of assessment (1 March 2023 to 29 February 2024); no equivalent incentive has replaced it (secondary source)

za-net-billing.title: South Africa - NERSA approved a net-billing framework in December 2024, but rollout runs municipality by municipality: Cape Town, eThekwini and Ekurhuleni have mature net metering/billing programmes, most others do not yet (secondary source)

za-sseg-registration.title: South Africa - Small-Scale Embedded Generation registration via PV GreenCard or the local municipality, requiring a Certificate of Compliance; Eskom simplified the compliance process and extended a fee waiver for systems up to 50 kW to March 2026

za-standards.title: South Africa - SANS 10142-1 (wiring) and SANS 60364-7-712 (solar PV installations) are the national installation standards; inverters require an NRS 097-2-1 type-test certificate from an accredited laboratory, and installers must issue a Certificate of Compliance

ma-loi-82-21.title: Morocco - Law 82-21 on self-production of electricity, implementing decree published in Bulletin Officiel n. 7489 on 9 March 2026 and entering force 9 June 2026: self-producers may inject and resell surplus capped at 20% of annual production; ANRE set buy-back tariffs of 0.18-0.21 DH/kWh for medium/high/very-high voltage, with no residential (BT, under 11 kW) tariff yet published (pv magazine France)

ma-import-duty.title: Morocco - import duty on assembled photovoltaic modules raised from 2.5% to 10% under the 2026 finance law to protect the domestic solar industry, while inverter duty fell from 17.5% to 2.5%

ma-nm-standards.title: Morocco - a commission of the Ministry of Energy, IMANOR, AMEE and IRESEN made 19 standards mandatory for photovoltaic installations, including NM CEI 61215 (module design), NM CEI 61730-2 (module safety qualification) and NM 10.1.001 (domestic and industrial PV installation)

br-lei-14300.title: Brazil - Lei 14.300/2022, the distributed generation legal framework: surplus injected to the grid earns kWh credits valid for 60 months; systems connected before 7 January 2023 keep full compensation until 2045, while newer systems phase in the Fio B distribution charge, reaching 45% of TUSD by 2025 and depreciating injected-kWh value by roughly 12.2% (secondary source)

br-import-tariff-25.title: Brazil - Resolution Gecex No. 666 raised the import tariff on photovoltaic modules from 9.6% to 25% for imports outside the quota system, effective from 2025/2026; a reduced 9.6% rate survives only for centralised projects over 5 MW within a capped quota, which does not apply to behind-the-meter residential imports

br-inmetro-nbr.title: Brazil - INMETRO Portaria 140 requires certification of PV generation, conditioning and storage equipment installed in buildings; ABNT NBR 16690 (2019) sets design requirements for the DC side of PV installations, including cabling, breakers, connectors and inverter ground-fault indication aligned to IEC 62109-2

pk-import-duty.title: Pakistan - solar panels carry 0% customs duty under Statutory Regulatory Orders promoting renewable energy; a 10% General Sales Tax applies from 1 July 2025 (a domestic consumption tax, not a border tariff), with a proposed rise to 18% dropped in the 2026-27 federal budget (secondary source)

bd-import-duty-zero.title: Bangladesh - import duty, regulatory duty, supplementary duty and advance tax on solar equipment reduced to zero in the FY2026-27 national budget, effective until 30 June 2031; previously combined PV import taxes ranged from 26.2% to 58.6%

id-sef-grant.title: Indonesia - the Ministry of Energy's Sustainable Energy Fund (SEF) grant covers 10% to nearly 100% of rooftop solar investment cost as a results-based payment after installation, open to residential, business, industrial and social PLN customer groups (UNDP / ESDM)

bd-idcol.title: Bangladesh - IDCOL has financed nearly 50% of the country's renewable energy capacity including domestic and industrial rooftop solar, and targets 6 GWp of further renewable finance over five years, but operates as an infrastructure financier rather than a universally accessible retail household loan product (secondary source)

pk-sbp-financing.title: Pakistan - the State Bank of Pakistan's Financing Scheme for Renewable Energy channels subsidised-rate lending for solar through commercial banks; several banks including Meezan Bank offer solar-specific loan and instalment products (SBP / secondary source)

mx-interconnection.title: Mexico - CRE-regulated distributed generation for installations under 500 kW offers three interconnection schemes since 2017: net metering (medicion neta), net billing (facturacion neta) and total energy sale, with a regulatory trend toward market-price surplus sale rather than 1:1 credit (secondary source)

mx-cenace-timeline.title: Mexico - CENACE has 30 business days to complete an interconnection study once payment is confirmed, under the distributed generation framework for installations under 500 kW (secondary source)

mx-nom-standards.title: Mexico - NOM-001-SEDE is the official standard for photovoltaic installations and CFE interconnection (Article 690 covers PV systems, Article 705 covers interconnection and equipment approval); inverters must be certified to NMX-J-643-ANCE (secondary source)

ke-self-consumption.title: Kenya - self-generation for own consumption below 1 MW does not require an EPRA licence under the Energy Act 2019; a signed net-metering agreement with KPLC is only needed for systems that export surplus to the grid

ch-feedin-2026.title: Switzerland - the revised Electricity Supply Act (StromVG), approved by referendum 9 June 2024, harmonises feed-in remuneration nationwide from 2026 based on a quarterly reference market price published by the Federal Office of Energy; since 1 January 2025 a virtual ZEV option lets consumers share locally consumed solar within the same building complex at a discounted grid fee (secondary source)

ch-nin-niv.title: Switzerland - NIN (Niederspannungs-Installationsnorm), maintained by Electrosuisse, is the national low-voltage installation standard for electrical work including PV; a restricted installation permit under Article 14 of the Low-Voltage Installation Ordinance (NIV) is legally required to carry out solar installation work

ch-solarprofi.title: Switzerland - Swissolar's Solarprofi quality label requires installers, planners and manufacturers to meet education and reference-project criteria and to keep attending courses to retain it, alongside Electrosuisse's regular NIN training courses

no-enova-2025.title: Norway - Enova pays 2,500 NOK per installed kW up to 15 kW (up to 37,500 NOK) for residential solar as of August 2025, open nationally to private homeowners applying in their own name; pre-approval required from 1 September 2025 (secondary source)

no-plusskunde.title: Norway - the plusskunde scheme lets producers sell excess electricity at the Nord Pool spot price minus a markup, exempt from the fixed component of production grid fees; the 100 kW production limit was removed from 1 January 2024, and self-produced, self-consumed electricity avoids grid fees and taxes entirely (secondary source)

ke-self-consumption-fee.title: Kenya - grid-interconnection fees and meter installation costs apply to net-metering (exporting) customers; self-generation under 1 MW for the owner's own consumption is exempt from EPRA licensing and therefore from these agreement-linked fees (secondary source, cross-referenced with EPRA licensing guide)

ke-tvet-training.title: Kenya - roughly 16 tertiary institutions nationally offer NITA and TVET CDACC-accredited solar PV training leading to recognised T1/T2/T3 technician licenses, which ERC requires for certification

pk-self-consumption-license.title: Pakistan - as of 2026, a NEPRA generation licence (fee waived for systems up to 25 kW) is required only for net-metering customers exporting to the grid; households running solar for self-consumption only, with no grid export, face no licensing requirement or fee (Dawn / Pakistan Observer)

ca-tariff-china.title: Canada - a 25% surtax applies to Chinese-origin solar panels as part of Canada's trade rebalancing with China, alongside batteries, semiconductors and critical minerals; since China supplies most imported panels, this is the tariff facing a typical importer regardless of the general 0-25% MFN range that applies by HS code (secondary source)

ca-self-consumption.title: Canada - zero-export, behind-the-meter configurations are an established option (Ontario's HRS program is one example), and no province bars self-consumption; CSA C22.1 Section 64 governs both grid-tied and self-consumption PV installations nationally (secondary source)

ca-red-seal.title: Canada - the interprovincial Red Seal Program sets common electrician certification standards recognised in every province and territory; several colleges (BCIT, NSCC, and the national Colleges and Institutes Canada programme) offer solar PV microcredentials specifically for Red Seal electricians

tr-net-metering.title: Turkey - post-2019 unlicensed rooftop solar uses monthly net metering with hourly netting introduced in November 2025 amendments; surplus after netting is purchased at 90% of the YEKDEM tariff applicable to licensed generation, and surplus can now be marketed through an aggregator (Mondaq / Pragma International legal briefings)

tr-connection.title: Turkey - unlicensed rooftop applications up to 3 MW are approved immediately if compliant, but overall assessment runs up to 20 days (plus a further 10 if documents are missing) followed by a 15-day window to execute the connection agreement; rooftop installations also need a municipal building permit and electrical project approval (secondary legal summary)

tr-china-antidumping.title: Turkey - anti-dumping measures on Chinese-origin solar modules can add roughly $25 per square metre on top of the general 0-5% tariff most other origins face (EU-origin panels enter duty-free under the Customs Union); since China supplies most imported modules globally, this is the tariff facing a typical importer

th-factory-license.title: Thailand - a Ministerial Regulation effective 28 December 2024 eliminated the factory licence (Ror Ngor 4) requirement from the ERC for rooftop solar outside industrial estates at any capacity; self-consumption installations now need only a PEA/MEA grid connection permit (Hunton Andrews Kurth legal briefing)

th-net-billing.title: Thailand - the net billing programme pays a fixed 2.20 THB/kWh for 10 years, with residential (Type 1, up to 10 kWp) export capped at 5 kW per meter; the NEPC expanded the programme to 500 MW and the ERC reopened a residential round on 1 July 2026 after a freeze, with commercial operation required by 2027 (capsolar / Sahawatthanakit legal summaries)

answers.note: Article 11 of Directive (EU) 2019/944 gives every final customer the right to a dynamic price contract from any supplier with more than 200,000 customers, but only once a smart meter is installed. ACER and CEER's 2024 retail monitoring confirms the score of 1 with market evidence rather than legal inference: fewer than 30% of households can access dynamic contracts in 10 member states, and fixed or regulated contracts still dominate in 15. Availability is real but far from universal.
Annex I requires bills to break the price into energy/supply, network, and taxes/levies/fees, using the common definitions in Regulation (EU) 2016/1952 across the Union.

Articles 20–23 require smart meters to provide validated historical consumption data and non-discriminatory electronic access to it. Scored 1 because entitlement follows smart meter installation, and rollout is incomplete in most member states.

Article 17 requires member states to allow demand response through aggregation to participate in all electricity markets alongside producers, and lets independent aggregators enter without other participants' consent. Scored 1 rather than 2 because the share of markets genuinely open to aggregated behind-the-meter technology depends on national prequalification rules that have not been checked country by country.

Article 32 requires a regulatory framework incentivising DSOs to procure flexibility, including from distributed generation and storage, where it defers network reinforcement. Scored 1 because regulators may derogate where procurement is not economically efficient, and CEER records derogations in practice, so this is not yet business as usual everywhere.

Article 21(2)(a) entitles renewables self-consumers to be free of any charges or fees on self-generated renewable electricity that remains within their premises. Charges may only fall on electricity fed into or taken from the grid.
Article 21(1) requires member states to ensure consumers are entitled to become renewables self-consumers, free of discriminatory or disproportionate procedures.

Article 17 requires a simple-notification procedure for self-consumer installations of 10.8 kW or less: notify the DSO, and connect if there is no reasoned refusal within one month. That is fit-and-inform.

Same simple-notification procedure. Connection follows a notification rather than an application, with deemed approval after one month; refusal is only permitted on justified safety or technical-incompatibility grounds.

The EU applies 0% duty to photovoltaic modules and 2.7% to lithium-ion batteries, both below the 10% threshold for full marks. Applies union-wide as the Common Customs Tariff, so this is not really a per-country judgement.
Article 18(3) requires certification or equivalent qualification schemes for installers of small-scale solar PV, based on the criteria in Annex IV, with mutual recognition between member states.

The Cheaper Home Batteries Program cuts roughly 30% off the upfront cost of small-scale batteries from 1 July 2025, delivered through the Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme that already underwrites rooftop solar. Available to households and small businesses nationally, so it meets the 'available to all customers' test.

Time-of-use retail tariffs are widely offered, but depend on a smart meter. The AEMC's 28 November 2024 final rule targets 100% smart meter deployment across the NEM by 2030, which is an explicit acknowledgement that coverage is not yet universal. Scored 1 until it is.

The AEMC's August 2021 DER determination removed the prohibition on export tariffs and required networks to provide a free basic export level, with the AER's Export Tariff Guidelines governing two-way pricing. Export pricing therefore exists, but is not a time-of-day market open on equal terms to both solar and storage, so scored 1.
The same rule package introduces customer access to real-time and historical smart meter data. Scored 1 because access follows smart meter installation, and the rollout runs to 2030.
AS/NZS 4777.2:2020 sets national inverter and installation requirements, enforced through SAA accreditation and periodically revised.
SAA compliance procedures audit installations against Australian Standards and scheme guidelines as a condition of accreditation.

Solar Accreditation Australia has operated the national installer and designer accreditation scheme under the SRES since 29 February 2024, covering grid-connected PV, battery storage and stand-alone systems. Accreditation is mandatory to create certificates under the scheme.

The AER's ring-fencing guideline prohibits distributors from providing contestable services with a battery unless they obtain a waiver, so network businesses cannot freely own behind-the-meter technology. They remain able to contract with and incentivise third-party behind-the-meter technology for network support, so this is 'some barriers' rather than significant ones.

AEMO publishes dispatch prices for energy and all FCAS markets every five minutes, free and public, alongside demand, generation, bids and interconnector flows. Fully transparent and in real time, which is the test for full marks.

AEMO operates eight separate FCAS markets covering regulation and contingency raise and lower services. Small resources reach them through registered aggregators, and third-party aggregators are established participants.

The RERT pays availability and activation payments for demand reduction, and aggregated smaller loads are explicitly eligible. Scored 1 because it is a last-resort emergency mechanism procured through a pre-qualified panel rather than a market open to all consumer participants.
Demand reduction is compensated through the RERT panel, but access runs through tender and pre-agreed contracts rather than being open to all customers.

South Australia set a record minimum operational demand of −209 MW on 19 October 2024, with rooftop PV meeting 64% of demand - regionally past the 70% test at times. Scored 1 for Australia as a whole because the NEM-wide distributed share remains well below that level, and this is exactly the divergence a national score conceals.

CSIP-AUS provides a national DER communications profile built on the IEEE 2030.5 international standard, with Clean Energy Council inverter certification against it. Scored 1 rather than 2 because it was developed by an industry working group rather than set by the system operator, and DNSP adoption is uneven - Queensland has offered dynamic connections since late 2022 while other networks lag.
The same profile governs DER data exchange, including dynamic operating envelope extensions. Uneven network adoption keeps this at partially national rather than universal.
Australia applies 0% import duty to solar panels and photovoltaic modules, well below the 10% threshold. GST applies but is a consumption tax, not a border tariff.
Accreditation rests on nationally recognised UEE units of competency delivered by registered training organisations in multiple states, offered continuously rather than to an occasional schedule.

South Australia reached a record minimum operational demand of −209 MW on 19 October 2024, with rooftop PV meeting 64% of demand and AEMO projecting 84%. AEMO is already operating this region beyond the 70% behind-the-meter threshold, which is why South Australia scores 2 where Australia as a whole scores 1.

FERC Order 2222 requires every RTO/ISO to open all wholesale services to DER aggregations regardless of size. Scored 1 rather than 2 because it is largely not yet operational: PJM's energy and ancillary services implementation is set for February 2028 and SPP's for Q2 2030, so in most of the country the barrier is scheduled to fall rather than fallen.

Order 2222 establishes the right of DER aggregations - the US equivalent of a VPP - to participate in wholesale markets. Scored 1 because access depends on each RTO's compliance tariff, and most implementation dates are still in the future.

IEEE 1547-2018 is a national technical standard with UL 1741 SB certification behind it, but it binds only where a state regulator or ISO has adopted it, and IREC tracks adoption dates state by state. National standard, localised force - so partially rather than universally adopted.
The same standard governs DER communications and interoperability, with the same state-by-state adoption pattern.
Inverters are certified to UL 1741, which incorporates IEEE 1547/1547.1 testing. Both are maintained national standards aligned to international practice.
UL 1741 listing is a safety certification requirement for grid-connected inverters nationwide, revised alongside IEEE 1547.

Section 201 safeguard tariffs expired on 6 February 2026, but antidumping and countervailing duty orders imposed on Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam in June 2025 remain, at rates from 9% to 292% depending on origin and producer. Since those four countries supply most imported cells and modules, the effective border cost sits well above the 25% mark.

The One Big Beautiful Bill Act terminated the section 25D residential clean energy credit for expenditures after 31 December 2025, so a household installing solar or storage in 2026 gets no federal credit, while utility-scale technology retains its own credits. Consumer-side incentives no longer match utility-scale ones.

The Self-Generation Incentive Program pays $200–$1,000/kWh toward storage, but as of April 2026 the residential budgets are fully reserved and new applications go on a waitlist. Available, but not universally accessible.

The Net Billing Tariff compensates exports at hourly avoided cost rather than a flat retail credit, so export value varies by time of day. It applies to all new PG&E, SCE and SDG&E customers and to both solar and paired storage.
Rule 21 requires an interconnection application, but Integration Capacity Analysis results now feed the Fast Track process and support automation. Simple and online rather than fit-and-inform.

PG&E, SCE and SDG&E each publish interactive ICA maps showing DER hosting capacity across thousands of distribution circuits, updated monthly, and the published values are the ones used to evaluate an application.

NY-Sun pays a declining megawatt-block incentive by region, but each block closes once fully subscribed, so support depends on where and when a household applies rather than being universally available.

The VDER Value Stack compensates exports by when and where they are delivered, stacking energy, capacity, environmental, demand reduction and locational system relief value. That is time-varying export pricing rather than a flat credit, and it is open to storage as well as solar.

The Locational System Relief Value pays DERs extra for siting in grid-constrained areas, and the Demand Reduction Value pays for cutting peak load. Both are standing tariff components rather than trials, which is what deferring network reinforcement through a market signal looks like in practice.
The Demand Reduction Value component of the Value Stack compensates peak demand reduction as part of the standard tariff.

The Standardized Interconnection Requirements give one statewide process and application for distributed generation and storage up to 5 MW, most recently revised effective 1 August 2025. An application is still required, so this is simple and standardised rather than fit-and-inform.
New York is one of the states that mandate utility hosting capacity analyses, published as maps by the Joint Utilities and refined under commission direction.

Texas has no statewide net metering requirement. Some retailers offer buyback at below retail value and Denton Municipal Electric is a lone exception, but there is no general entitlement to be paid for exports.

ERCOT's Aggregate DER pilot, in Phase 3 as of 2025, lets aggregated distribution-level resources follow ERCOT dispatch through retail electricity providers. Still a pilot with capacity caps rather than open market access.

Battery Bonus closed to new participants on 1 July 2024 and was replaced by Bring Your Own Device and BYOD Plus from 15 May 2025. Incentives exist but run in capacity-capped tranches rather than being open to all customers continuously.

The Smart DER export programme, approved by the Hawaii PUC, pays for exports on time-differentiated tracks, with legacy Customer Grid Supply, CGS Plus and Smart Export customers transitioning onto it from 1 October 2024. Open to solar and paired storage.
BYOD pays solar-plus-storage customers to discharge during the evening peak, which is peak demand reduction compensated as standard programme design.
BYOD Plus dispatches customer batteries in response to system need, compensating demand reduction as business as usual.
Hawaii mandates utility hosting capacity analyses, among the earliest states to do so.
The SMART programme pays a per-kWh incentive for 20 years on top of net metering, available statewide to residential solar owners rather than rationed by block or waitlist.
Exports are credited through net metering at retail value with a flat SMART adder. Compensation exists and is open to all, but it does not vary by time of day.
ConnectedSolutions pays roughly $225/kW of average summer performance for battery discharge across 30–60 peak events, open to any customer with a qualifying battery.
The same programme compensates dispatched demand reduction as an ongoing offer rather than a trial.

PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, announced 15 February 2024, pays ₹30,000/kW up to 2 kW and ₹18,000/kW above that, capped at ₹78,000. A national residential scheme open to households generally, which meets the test for reducing upfront cost for all customers.

Net metering is available through the local DISCOM as part of the scheme, offsetting imports against exports each billing cycle. It is a volumetric offset rather than time-of-day export pricing, and availability depends on DISCOM approval.

Basic customs duty on modules fell to 20% from 2 February 2025, but a 20% AIDC applies on top, putting the combined rate at about 40%, with anti-dumping duties of up to 30% recommended on Chinese cells and modules in September 2025. Well above the 25% threshold.

Net metering has operated under the NEPRA 2015 distributed generation regulations, but the December 2025 revision moves new prosumers to net billing at a fixed Rs11/unit against Rs22 for existing agreements, and cuts agreement terms from seven years to five. Export compensation exists but is being narrowed and is not time-of-day.

The Net Metering Guidelines 2018, amended in 2019 to cover all three-phase consumers, allow rooftop exports against consumption. Meters must be bi-directional and time-of-use capable, but compensation is a volumetric offset rather than time-varying export pricing.
All equipment including modules and inverters must be SREDA-approved and meet Bangladesh Standards and equivalent IEC standards, so a national standard aligned to international norms is in force.

Soorya Bala Sangramaya promotes rooftop solar across households, religious premises, hotels and industry through SLSEA with CEB and LECO. It provides a route to installation but is a promotion programme rather than a universal low-cost finance or rebate entitlement.

Customers choose between Net Metering, Net Accounting - where CEB or LECO buys surplus at a set feed-in tariff - and Net Plus. Export compensation is available to all rooftop customers but is not time-of-day priced.

Shift and Save prices daytime, overnight and evening peak at roughly 1:2:3, but it ran as a 16,000-customer pilot on two islands and closed to new enrolments on 1 February 2025. Existing participants keep the rate, so time-of-use pricing reaches some customers rather than all.

The DPU requires every investor-owned distribution company to interconnect under a common Model DG Interconnection Tariff, with Simplified and Expedited paths for smaller facilities. Standardised statewide and application-based rather than fit-and-inform.

KfW programme 270 lends up to 100% of the cost of a PV system or battery over terms up to 30 years, is open nationally rather than rationed by block or waitlist, and can be combined with regional grants and the EEG tariff.

KfW 270 starts at roughly 3.98% effective per year, below the 5% threshold for full marks. This replaces the World Bank lending-rate proxy, which has no figure for Germany in any case: euro-area countries largely do not report that indicator.

The EEG pays a feed-in tariff fixed for 20 years from commissioning, with distinct rates for surplus feed-in and full feed-in. Available to every rooftop operator and to storage-paired systems, but a fixed rate rather than time-of-day export pricing.
The Marktstammdatenregister is a single national online register. Registration is free, takes 15–30 minutes, and is required within a month of commissioning under §71 EEG 2023.

The prime à l'autoconsommation - the only state subsidy toward the cost of a PV installation - was abolished in early June 2026 for new self-consumption-with-surplus installations. Photovoltaic panels are not covered by MaPrimeRénov', and the zero-rate eco-loan and 5.5% VAT reach solar thermal rather than PV. Installations connected before 5 June 2026 keep the old terms for 20 years.

EDF OA buys surplus under the obligation d'achat, but the rate for new installations fell to 1.1 c€/kWh HT on 5 June 2026 from 4 c€/kWh. Export compensation is available to all, at a fixed rate rather than by time of day.

A 50% income tax deduction on installation costs up to €96,000 applies to a first home through 31 December 2026, and 36% to other properties, recovered over ten annual instalments. Open to households generally rather than capped by a subscription block.

Scambio sul Posto closed to plants commissioned from 29 May 2025, so new installations use Ritiro Dedicato, under which the GSE buys surplus at a set price with a 2026 minimum guaranteed price of 4.75 c€/kWh. Available to all, but not time-of-day pricing.
IDAE grants cover 15–40% of installation cost, but are administered through the autonomous communities against limited budgets rather than being continuously available to every consumer.

Simplified surplus compensation under RD 244/2019 credits exports against imports within the same billing period for renewable installations up to 100 kW, applied by the supplier as a bill discount. No producer registration is needed, but it is a netting mechanism rather than time-of-day export pricing.

Installations must be notified to the distributor and, in cases including self-consumption without surplus, entered in the autonomous or state self-consumption registry. A registration process exists but runs through regional administration rather than one national digital register.

Households net exports against consumption under the salderingsregeling until 31 December 2026. From 1 January 2027 the scheme ends in a single step and suppliers must pay at least 50% of the basic supply tariff for exports until 2030. Compensation is universal but not time-of-day priced, and is about to fall sharply.

Mój Prąd pays up to 7,000 PLN toward a 2–10 kWp system and up to 16,000 PLN toward storage, but runs in time-limited editions: edition 6.0 covers investments completed by 31 October 2025, and the 2026 round is expected to focus on storage with PV funded only in transitional tenders or as part of a storage package.

Prosumers settle under net-billing, selling surplus at the market price published by URE and buying at the retail price. Market-linked export compensation open to all prosumers, though it tracks a published market price rather than offering a time-of-day tariff choice.

The Energy (Net-Metering) Regulations 2024 give consumers with renewable systems under 1 MW the right to export surplus and receive bill credits at the retail tariff, with domestic systems capped at 10 kW. Compensation is open to all consumers but is a retail-rate credit rather than time-of-day export pricing.

Net-metering connection requires an application to the utility with a 60-day approval window. That is well beyond the 15 days the rubric allows for a simple online process, so it scores 0 despite the framework itself being new and clear.

Modules must meet KS IEC 61215 for design qualification, and every consignment needs a KEBS Certificate of Conformity before shipment. National standards adopted directly from the international IEC series.
KS IEC 61730 governs module safety, enforced through KEBS conformity assessment, with separate standards for inverters, batteries and mounting systems.

Solar modules enter duty-free and VAT-exempt, but the rest of a behind-the-meter technology system does not: inverters attract 10% duty plus 16% VAT, and batteries and charge controllers are assessed separately. Since storage is as much a behind-the-meter technology as generation, the effective border cost sits in the 10–25% band rather than below 10%.

EPRA licenses solar PV technicians, contractors and vendors nationally, with technicians also registering with the Engineers Board of Kenya and holding a T3 solar technician certificate. A recognised national qualification is required to work legally.

Rooftop systems receive a fixed feed-in tariff for surplus exports - ¥24/kWh for four years then ¥8.3/kWh for residential under 10 kW - with a ¥1/kWh bonus once self-consumption reaches 30%. Open to all rooftop operators, but a scheduled tariff rather than time-of-day export pricing.

The Korea Energy Agency's new and renewable energy equipment fund provides concessional low-interest finance for systems up to 200 kW, and the Solar Rental Program adds low-interest loans and subsidies for residential and small commercial installations on a standing annual budget.

KEPCO nets surplus at retail rates for systems up to 50 kW residential and 1 MW commercial under a grid connection agreement. Universal in practice, but a retail-rate offset rather than time-of-day export pricing.

MEMR Regulation 2/2024 abolished net metering: exported electricity can no longer be counted against the bill, and the export-import kWh meter was replaced with an advanced meter. Users approved before the regulation keep the old scheme for ten years, but for anyone installing now there is no export compensation at all.

Connection is capped by a national quota - 5,746 MW across 2024–2028, allocated annually - so approval depends on quota availability rather than on meeting a technical standard. IESR assesses the arrangement as a barrier to rooftop deployment.

NEM 3.0 credits exports against the TNB bill, but capacity is released by SEDA in quota rounds and approval is not automatic on application, with applicants waitlisted once a round fills. Available, but not to all consumers on demand.

Publication of utility hosting capacity maps is mandated state by state, and IREC records only seven states requiring them. This is the default for states not on that list; those that are carry their own answer.
Nevada is among the states mandating utility hosting capacity analyses.
Minnesota is among the states mandating utility hosting capacity analyses.
Maryland requires utilities to publish solar hosting capacity maps.
New Jersey requires utilities to publish solar hosting capacity maps.
Connecticut requires utilities to publish solar hosting capacity maps.

Regulation 543/2013 requires TSOs to submit market data to the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform, which publishes it free of charge, in English, downloadable and kept for at least five years - including balancing energy prices and volumes activated. Scored 1 rather than 2 because publication is on statutory schedules rather than genuinely real time.

RED III Article 16 caps rooftop solar permitting at three months with tacit approval, and the recast EPBD requires new buildings permitted after 29 May 2026 to be solar-ready, with systems up to 100 kW decided within one month. Scored 1 rather than 2 because planning consent still restricts installation in conservation areas and on protected buildings across most member states.

RED II Annex IV obliges member states to run certification or equivalent qualification schemes for small-scale renewable installers and to publish information about them, and the RES EU database records the schemes in force country by country. Scored 1 because the directive guarantees a scheme exists, not that courses are offered throughout a country on a regular basis.

Article 36 bars distribution system operators from owning, developing, managing or operating storage, so that storage services stay market-based. Derogations exist for fully integrated network components and where a regulator finds no market interest, and network operators may still contract with third-party behind-the-meter technology - so this is some barriers rather than significant ones.

Installers must calculate expected annual generation using the MCS Performance Estimate methodology, and every MCS-certified installer must belong to an approved consumer code - RECC, HIES or GGF - covering sales practice, written contracts, deposit protection and accurate performance estimates. Standards exist and are enforced through certification rather than advisory.
MIS 3002 sets national installation, wiring, commissioning and handover requirements for solar PV, aligned to BS 7671 and revised periodically - version 5.0 was published in 2025.
The same standard carries the safety requirements, enforced as a condition of MCS certification, which is in turn a condition of access to consumer support schemes.
MCS certification is the recognised national qualification route for solar PV installers, requiring compliance with MIS 3002 and membership of an approved consumer code.

ComEd and Ameren pay an upfront Distributed Generation rebate of $300/kW DC for solar and $300/kWh for storage to residential customers installing a smart inverter, reducing capital cost at the point of purchase rather than over time.

Full retail net metering closed to new residential and small commercial systems on 1 January 2025; new customers receive supply-only net metering, and taking the DG rebate permanently forfeits any grandfathered full-retail status. Export compensation remains universal but is materially reduced and is not time-of-day priced.

Export compensation runs on net billing at the Resource Comparison Proxy rate, set annually by the Arizona Corporation Commission and locked for ten years at installation with reductions capped at 10% a year. Available to all customers of the regulated utilities, but a fixed avoided-cost rate rather than time-of-day export pricing.

HB2301 requires every municipality and county to offer instant solar permitting from 1 January 2026, with the largest jurisdictions accepting SolarAPP+ for same-day residential permits. Automated permitting replacing local discretion is exactly what the top tier describes.

Applications go through the PM Surya Ghar national portal and are routed electronically to the DISCOM for feasibility approval. A simple online process, but approval is still required before installation rather than fit-and-inform.
Registration is handled digitally through the national portal, which covers consumer applications, vendor registration and DISCOM routing in one national system.

Vendors registering under PM Surya Ghar must show at least three technical personnel trained under Suryamitra or certified by the Skill Council for Green Jobs, making a recognised national qualification a condition of participating in the scheme.

SLSEA publishes rooftop installation guidelines and a standard specification for hybrid inverter safety, and requires conformity certificates for panels, inverters and DC cables backed by accredited laboratory test certificates.
Solar service providers must register with SLSEA under published terms, maintain safety policies and safe working practices, and appear in the national registered provider directory.

Self-consumed electricity itself is not charged, but getting there costs money: a municipal building permit of roughly $50–$500 and a TDU interconnection agreement. The fee is payable to the permitting authority rather than to the grid incumbent, which is the middle tier rather than the zero case. Interconnection rules also apply the same process to a 5 kW rooftop system as to a 250 kW commercial one.

Every state operates interconnection procedures for distributed energy resources, built on IEEE 1547 and UL 1741 certification, which presupposes that consumers may connect and self-consume. No US jurisdiction bars behind-the-meter self-consumption; what varies is the compensation for exports and the cost of getting connected, which other questions capture.

The Solar Rights Act voids any property owners' association rule prohibiting a solar energy device, and HB 431 extended it to solar roof tiles in 2025. Associations may still impose reasonable conditions - panels within the roofline, following the roof slope, standard frame colours - and municipal permitting applies, so restrictions persist in particular locations rather than having been removed.

Installation is governed by the harmonised European adoption of the IEC series: EN IEC 61215 for module design qualification, EN IEC 62109 for converter safety, and HD 60364-7-712 for the electrical installation of PV in buildings, including earthing and surge protection. Maintained through CENELEC and revised in step with IEC, so aligned to international best practice by construction.

EN IEC 61730-1 and 61730-2 are harmonised standards under the Low Voltage Directive, cited in the Official Journal, so conformity carries a presumption of compliance and CE marking is mandatory. Modules above 75 V DC additionally fall under the EMC Directive and RoHS.

The Canada Greener Homes Loan offered $40,000 interest-free over ten years but closed to new applications on 2 October 2025. Its replacement, the Greener Homes Affordability Program, is restricted to low- and median-income households and delivered provincially with solar eligibility varying, so support exists but is no longer open to all consumers.

Every province and territory operates net metering, called micro-generation in Alberta and Yukon, with system caps from 10 kW in Nunavut to 5 MW in Alberta. Compensation is a retail-rate credit rather than time-of-day export pricing, and annual surpluses are typically settled at wholesale.
Section 64 of the Canadian Electrical Code governs PV installations nationally, setting DC voltage limits and wiring methods, and is adopted by every province through its electrical safety regime.

Every piece of equipment in a Canadian solar installation - modules, inverters, racking, rapid shutdown and arc-fault devices - must carry a certification mark from a Standards Council of Canada accredited body.

The Indian Energy Exchange publishes day-ahead and real-time market clearing prices and traded volumes, with real-time data published in 15-minute blocks. Regulated by CERC and public since 2008, so transparent and effectively real time.

CEA's 2013 connectivity regulations and 2010 safety regulations set national installation requirements, with BIS IS 16221 for inverters and IS 14086 for modules - the latter mandatory nationwide under the 2022 Quality Control Order.
The CEA (Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations 2010 carry the safety requirements, enforced alongside mandatory BIS certification of installed equipment.

Consumers may connect behind-the-meter technology for self-consumption nationwide; there is no ban. The rubric here is binary, so the state-variable sanctioned-load caps noted in the source (Kerala proposed as low as 3 kW, most states up to 100% of sanctioned load) are recorded as a caveat rather than a partial score.

Net metering applications must go through an AEDB-registered installer and take 30–90 days from application to commissioning depending on the DISCO. Well beyond the 15-day threshold for the simple-and-online tier.
NEPRA and DISCOs require modules certified to IEC 61215/61730 and inverters compliant with IEEE 1547/UL 1741/IEC 62116, including mandatory anti-islanding protection.
The same certification regime carries the safety requirement, enforced through NEPRA and DISCO inspection of every net-metering installation.

Installers must hold AEDB competency certification (Category V1/V2 and above) and Pakistan Engineering Council registration to submit net-metering applications, making a recognised national qualification a legal precondition of practising.

CEB's interconnection guide requires inverters to meet IEEE 1547/UL 1741 or IEC 62109 with anti-islanding protection, and commissioning is tested against IEC 61727, IEEE 1547-2018 and the IET 18th Edition wiring regulations.

Distribution utilities issue an approval letter within 10 working days of application, under the 15-day threshold for the simple tier. Scored 1 rather than 2 because an application and inspection are still required and the process is not established as an online one.
Solar PV training in Bangladesh runs through occasional workshops and short private courses rather than a standing nationwide programme offered regularly in multiple locations.

SARS offered a 25% rebate on solar panel cost up to R15,000, but only for panels first used within the 2024 tax year (1 March 2023 to 29 February 2024). No successor scheme has been introduced, so no low-cost finance or rebate route is currently available to residential customers.

NERSA approved a national net-billing framework in December 2024, but implementation is municipal: Cape Town, eThekwini and Ekurhuleni have mature programmes while most other municipalities and Eskom-direct customers do not yet. Export compensation exists but is not available to all customers.

SSEG registration runs through the PV GreenCard digital platform or the local municipality and requires a Certificate of Compliance rather than a notify-and-connect model. Eskom simplified the process and extended a registration fee waiver to March 2026, but an application and inspection are still required.
PV GreenCard operates as a national digital SSEG registration platform used across municipalities, rather than a paper-based or purely local process.
SANS 10142-1 and SANS 60364-7-712 set national wiring and PV installation requirements, with NERSA-approved grid codes governing connection.

Inverters require an NRS 097-2-1 type-test certificate from an accredited laboratory, and installers must issue a Certificate of Compliance confirming the installation meets national safety standards.

Law 82-21's implementing decree, effective 9 June 2026, lets self-producers resell surplus capped at 20% of annual production. ANRE has set buy-back tariffs for medium and high voltage systems, but no residential low-voltage tariff has been published yet, and the rate is fixed rather than time-of-day.

The 2026 finance law raised the import duty on assembled PV modules from 2.5% to 10% to protect domestic manufacturing, landing exactly at the boundary between the top and middle tier; inverter duty fell to 2.5% over the same period.

A joint commission of the Ministry of Energy, IMANOR, AMEE and IRESEN made 19 standards mandatory for PV installations, including NM CEI 61215 for module design and NM 10.1.001 for domestic and industrial installation - a national standard set aligned to the IEC series.
NM CEI 61730-2, part of the same mandatory standard set, specifically defines safety qualification requirements for PV module operation.

Lei 14.300 credits surplus generation as kWh valid for 60 months. Systems connected before 7 January 2023 keep full compensation until 2045, but newer systems face the progressively phased-in Fio B distribution charge, which reaches 45% of TUSD by 2025 and cuts the effective value of injected energy by around 12%. A banking mechanism open to all, but not time-of-day export pricing, and its value is being deliberately eroded for new entrants.

Resolution Gecex 666 raised the import tariff on PV modules from 9.6% to 25% for imports outside the quota system. A reduced 9.6% rate survives only for centralised projects above 5 MW within a capped quota, which does not reach behind-the-meter residential imports, so the tariff actually facing a household is 25%.

ABNT NBR 16690 (2019) sets national design requirements for the DC side of PV installations - cabling, breakers, connectors and disconnect switches - maintained by the national standards body and periodically revised.

INMETRO Portaria 140 requires certification of generation, conditioning and storage equipment installed in buildings, and NBR 16690 mandates inverter ground-fault detection and external alarm indication aligned to IEC 62109-2.

Solar panels carry 0% customs duty under SROs promoting renewable energy. A 10% GST applies from 1 July 2025, but that is a domestic consumption tax rather than a border tariff, which is what this question asks about.
The FY2026-27 national budget zeroed import duty, regulatory duty, supplementary duty and advance tax on solar equipment until 30 June 2031, down from a combined 26.2-58.6% previously.

The Sustainable Energy Fund grant covers 10% to nearly 100% of rooftop solar investment cost, paid after installation, and is open to residential as well as business, industrial and social PLN customer groups.

IDCOL has financed nearly half of Bangladesh's renewable energy capacity, including domestic rooftop solar, and targets 6 GWp further over five years. It operates as an infrastructure and project financier rather than a retail product a household can straightforwardly apply for, so finance exists but is not clearly available to all consumers on the same terms.

The State Bank of Pakistan directs commercial banks to offer subsidised-rate renewable energy financing, and several banks including Meezan Bank offer solar-specific loan products. Available but channelled through individual banks' own eligibility and terms rather than a universal scheme.

Distributed generation under 500 kW can use net metering, net billing or total energy sale, all CRE-regulated and available nationally, but none price exports by time of day, and the regulatory trend is toward market-price surplus sale rather than 1:1 crediting.

CENACE has 30 business days to complete an interconnection study once payment is confirmed, for installations under 500 kW - beyond the 15-day threshold for the simple-and-online tier, though the process is standardised nationally rather than locally variable.
NOM-001-SEDE is the national standard for photovoltaic installations, with Article 690 covering PV systems and Article 705 covering CFE interconnection and equipment approval requirements.
Interactive inverters must be certified to NMX-J-643-ANCE before they can be used for interconnection, enforced as part of the national standard.

Self-generation for the owner's own consumption below 1 MW is explicitly exempt from EPRA licensing under the Energy Act 2019. No barrier to connecting for self-consumption; only exporting surplus requires a separate net-metering agreement.

From 2026 feed-in remuneration is harmonised nationwide and linked to a quarterly reference market price rather than a flat utility-set rate, and a virtual ZEV option since January 2025 lets neighbours share locally consumed solar at a discounted grid fee. Scored 1 rather than 2 because the reference price resets quarterly, not by time of day.
NIN, maintained by Electrosuisse, is the national low-voltage electrical installation standard covering PV work, reviewed and updated as part of a standing national body's remit.
A restricted installation permit under NIV Article 14 is a legal precondition for carrying out solar installation work, enforced nationally rather than left to local discretion.
The NIV Article 14 restricted permit functions as the national recognised qualification required to install and maintain solar systems.

Electrosuisse runs regular NIN and NIV preparatory courses nationally, and Swissolar's Solarprofi label requires ongoing course attendance to retain, so training is available on a standing, countrywide basis rather than a single location or infrequent schedule.
Enova pays 2,500 NOK per installed kW up to 15 kW, worth up to 37,500 NOK, open nationally to private homeowners rather than rationed by region or waitlist.

Plusskunde exports are paid at the Nord Pool spot price minus a markup, which moves hourly with the wholesale market - genuinely time-of-day pricing rather than a flat rate. Open nationally since the 100 kW production cap was removed in January 2024.
Self-produced electricity that is self-consumed is exempt from grid fees and taxes entirely under the plusskunde arrangement, with grid charges applying only to electricity bought from the grid.
NEK 400/410 is the national electrical installation standard, and Enova support requires installation by an electrician with the corresponding authorisation.
The same NEK 400/410 authorisation requirement carries the safety standard, enforced as a condition of both legal installation and Enova support.

Grid-interconnection and metering fees apply to net-metering customers who export, but self-generation under 1 MW for the owner's own consumption is exempt from EPRA licensing entirely, so a self-consumption-only installation carries no such fee.

Around 16 tertiary institutions nationally offer NITA and TVET CDACC-accredited solar PV training leading to T1/T2/T3 licenses, which ERC requires for recognised certification - regular and geographically spread rather than a single location or infrequent course.

A NEPRA generation licence, with its fee waived for systems up to 25 kW, is required only for net-metering customers exporting to the grid. Self-consumption-only installations face no licensing requirement or fee.

Households running solar purely for self-consumption, without grid export, face no NEPRA licensing requirement - only net-metering (export) participants are regulated. No barrier to connecting for self-consumption.

Zero-export, behind-the-meter configurations are an established option nationally - Ontario's HRS programme is one example - and CSA C22.1 Section 64 governs self-consumption PV installations the same as grid-tied ones. No province bars connecting for self-consumption.

A 25% surtax applies specifically to Chinese-origin solar panels, and China supplies most imported modules, so the tariff actually facing a typical importer sits at the top of the rubric's bracket regardless of the lower general MFN range that applies to other HS codes.

The interprovincial Red Seal Program sets one nationally recognised electrician certification standard honoured in every province and territory, letting a certified installer work anywhere in Canada without re-certifying.

Solar PV microcredentials built for Red Seal electricians are offered at colleges across multiple provinces - BCIT, NSCC and the national Colleges and Institutes Canada programme among them - on a standing, regularly available basis.

Unlicensed rooftop solar nets consumption against production monthly, with hourly netting introduced by November 2025 amendments. Surplus is bought at a fixed 90% of the YEKDEM licensed-generation tariff rather than a market or time-of-day rate, so this is closer to a scheduled feed-in price than genuine time-of-use export pricing.

Systems up to 1 MW are licence-exempt and up to 3 MW get immediate approval if compliant, but the overall assessment window runs up to 20 days (30 if documents are missing) plus a 15-day connection-agreement window, and rooftop installations still need a municipal building permit and electrical project approval. Simpler than a licensed project, but well beyond the 15-day threshold for the top tier.

Most origins face a 0-5% tariff and EU-origin panels are duty-free under the Customs Union, but anti-dumping measures add roughly $25/m2 on Chinese-origin modules - and China supplies most of the modules actually imported, so the tariff facing a typical importer sits well above the 25% threshold.

The net billing programme pays a fixed 2.20 THB/kWh for 10 years rather than a time-of-day rate, residential export is capped at 5 kW per meter, and the whole scheme runs in capacity-limited rounds (500 MW nationally) that were frozen and only reopened on 1 July 2026 - export compensation exists, but is rationed rather than open to every customer on demand.

The Ministerial Regulation effective 28 December 2024 removed the ERC factory licence requirement for rooftop solar outside industrial estates at any capacity. A self-consumption installation now needs only a grid connection permit from PEA or MEA, removing what had been the main regulatory barrier.

Self-consumption-only connection is simplified to a PEA/MEA grid permit following the December 2024 deregulation, but a system capable of exporting still goes through the separate, capacity-capped net billing application process rather than a fit-and-inform route, so the connection process as a whole is not yet at the top tier.
